title: Arcane
body: Portainer Business Edition Starter costs $1,045 a year. Arcane is open source Docker management that you host yourself, so someone on the team has to run it and keep it updated. The main branch is v3 now and the old 2.x line has its own branch. The last commit was today. There's nobody to call when it breaks.
verdict: If running your own Docker tooling doesn't scare you, you can cancel Portainer Business.
other_side: Keep paying if your team needs a vendor to call when something breaks.

title: Dograh
body:
Dograh is an open source voice AI platform with a visual workflow builder and telephony support. The README says self-hosting takes one Docker command.

Vapi's Core plan is $29 a month. Dograh isn't free either, because you run the server and bring your own keys for the LLM and the speech models. And when a live call drops, you're the one who has to deal with it.

It has 72 contributors and the last commit was yesterday.
verdict: If you build voice agents and can run Docker, try Dograh next to Vapi.
other_side: Keep paying if you don't want to run your own server and look after the provider keys yourself.

title: Hex
body:
Wispr Flow Pro is $12 per user a month. A team of ten pays $120.

Hex does the main thing. According to the README you hold a key and talk, and it transcribes on your device and pastes the text at the cursor. The first run downloads a speech model and after that nothing leaves the machine.

It's a young project, though 25 people have worked on it and the last commit was today. Upkeep is on you, and when it breaks there's nobody to call.
verdict: Use Hex alongside Wispr Flow for a few weeks before you cancel anything.
other_side: Keep paying if you want someone to call when dictation stops working.

facts.description: Local voice dictation for mac, windows and linux
facts.readme_excerpt: # Hex Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and it pastes. ## How it works - hold the shortcut, speak, then let go - Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in - the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine - experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar ## What it does - hold the shortcut to dictate, or set Shortcut mode to Tap to start and stop with a press - the text lands at the cursor in whatever app you're in - Option-Shift-V pastes the last dictation again (Ctrl-Alt-V on Windows and Linux) - History keeps your dictations, searchable, for 7 days by default - Output runs every dictation through steps you choose (word replacements, built-in cleanups, your own scripts, an optional OpenCode rewrite), with different steps per app or website - Vocabulary is one list of names Hex should know; Whisper and Qwen3-ASR read it while transcribing, Parakeet models read it with Labs › Vocabulary help on, and the OpenCode rewrite uses it - Annotate records the screen while you draw and talk, on macOS, Linux and Windows (GNOME Wayland needs Labs › Annotate on GNOME) - an authenticated local API and the [TypeScript SDK](sdk/typescript/README.md) transcribe with the same model, for your own tools - Meetings is a macOS lab that records a call and writes the transcript Output and History:     ## Speech models Hex downloads one model the first time it runs and transcribes wit
